judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Contractor pays royalties and defends infringement suits 'but shall not be responsible ... when a particular design, process or product of a particular manufacturer is required by the Contract Documents' — an exception whose trigger is often disputed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.5 makes royalties, defence costs and settlements a reimbursable Cost of the Work with its own exclusions, so cost-bearing and reimbursement are addressed twice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the fullest extent permitted by law', 'but only to the extent caused by the negligent acts or omissions', and 'regardless of whether or not such claim ... is caused in part by a party indemnified hereunder' are notoriously contested formulations in one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with 11.3.1-11.3.2's Project Management Protective Liability waiver (which is 'optional' and unaddressed in the blank Article 16), 11.4.7's waiver of subrogation and 4.3.10's waiver of consequential damages.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short anti-workers'-compensation-limitation clause in standard form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on 3.18.1 and 11.1.1.1; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of the Architect; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement identifies Fung/Howenson as Architect; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires written consent of Owner, Contractor and Architect to restrict or modify the Architect's duties, with consent not unreasonably withheld; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 adds an Owner consent requirement to every Architect approval and 4.2.13/12.2.3 shift decision timing, which arguably modifies the Architect's authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scanned text of the successor-Architect provision is scrambled to the point that the sentence cannot be read as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements 4.1.1 and 4.2; no substantive conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describes the Architect's role and limits authority to what the Documents provide 'unless otherwise modified in writing'; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 requires the Owner's express consent wherever the Architect's is required, which reshapes this administration role.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short disclaimer of the Architect's control over the Contractor's means and acts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.3.1 and Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1's parallel Owner disclaimer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A routing rule for communications with 'endeavor to communicate' as the operative verb — aspirational rather than mandatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 requires simultaneous written notice to the Owner, and Supplementary Condition 2.1.1.1 names who may act for the Owner, so the routing is modified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scanned text of the certification provision is fragmentary, leaving the Architect's certifying duty only partly legible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 9.4.1-9.4.2 and Agreement 12.1.9, which state the same duty more fully; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dense but standard limitation of the Architect's submittal review to conformance with the design concept; 'reasonable promptness' is the soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1 requires Architect approval of all shop drawings, which sits with rather than against this limitation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scanned sentence is broken and its cross-references ('Paragraph ... and 7.4') cannot be read with confidence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Corresponds to Article 7's Change Order machinery and Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1; consistent in substance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Badly scanned; the duties concerning Substantial Completion and the final Certificate can only be reconstructed from 9.8 and 9.10.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 conditions the final Certificate on Owner acceptance of warranties, and Agreement 12.2.3 sets its own timetable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Project representatives 'if the Owner and Architect agree'; the duties are to be set out elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No such written description appears in the enumerated documents, but nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable promptness' and a rule that no delay is recognised until fifteen days after written request combine an open standard with a hard deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 4.3.7.3-4.3.7.4 impose further requirements on time claims arising from such delays.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interpretations must be 'consistent with the intent of and reasonably inferable from the Contract Documents' and the Architect is not liable for decisions rendered 'in good faith' — both elastic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1 makes the Architect's interpretation, as approved by the Owner, the tie-breaker for inconsistencies, which enlarges this role.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Matters relating to aesthetic effect' has no boundary, yet decisions on them are made 'final if consistent with the intent expressed in the Contract Documents' — two indeterminate tests stacked.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.6.1 carves aesthetic-effect Claims out of arbitration entirely, so the scope of this term controls what a tribunal may hear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Claim' is defined broadly to include 'other disputes and matters in question ... arising out of or relating to the Contract', with written initiation required.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds the 21-day limits in 4.3.2, the Architect decision requirement in 4.4 and the arbitration route in 4.6, and Agreement 12.2.4 bypasses the Architect for final-accounting disputes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 21-day initiation period running from either the event or recognition of the condition, 'whichever is later' — a limitation whose start date is often fought over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.4 gives a different 30-day period for final-accounting disputes and 4.6.3 sets yet another arbitration deadline, so the claim clocks must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires continued performance and continued payment pending resolution; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subject to 9.7.1 and Article 14 stoppage rights, which it expressly excepts; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Differ materially', 'unusual nature' and 'generally recognized as inherent in construction activities of the character provided for' are the classic differing-site-conditions standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(b) bars extra compensation for dimensional differences and 7.1.3.1 bars adjustments absent a Change Order, both of which cut against this equitable-adjustment right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It lists six specific grounds for cost claims and closes with '(7) other reasonable grounds' — an open catch-all appended to enumerated specifics, the paradigm general-versus-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 confines increases to Change Orders, which narrows whatever '(7) other reasonable grounds' might otherwise reach.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires an estimate of cost and probable effect of delay; a single Claim suffices for continuing delay. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 4.3.7.3 adds detailed content requirements and 4.3.7.4 bars separate increases for concurrent causes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Abnormal for the period of time, could not have been reasonably anticipated and had an adverse effect' is a three-part standard resting entirely on judgment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with 8.3.1's extension right and Supplementary Condition 4.3.7.3's documentation rules; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Within a reasonable time not exceeding 21 days after discovery' pairs a standard with a cap; workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aligns with the 21-day regime in 4.3.2 and 4.3.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Materially changed' quantities causing 'substantial inequity' are open standards, and the adjustment is simply 'equitable'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 5.2.3 states no unit prices at all, so this provision has nothing to operate on unless Exhibits A-D are read as unit prices.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mutual consequential-damages waiver with enumerated categories and a saving for 'liquidated direct damages' — the enumerated lists and the profit carve-out ('except anticipated profit arising directly from the Work') are much-litigated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9.7.1 promises the Contractor's costs of shutdown, delay and start-up, Supplementary Condition 11.6 shifts attorneys' fees, and Agreement 13.1 computes a termination fee as if the Work were completed — all of which the waiver may or may not reach.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A ten-day menu of Architect responses ending with the Architect's 'sole discretion' to decline; clear if one-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.4 lets the Contractor demand arbitration of the final accounting 'without a further decision of the Architect', bypassing this step.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'May, but shall not be obligated to' consult; permissive and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.4.2 and 4.4.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A ten-day response procedure with three permitted answers; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.4.2; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Final and binding on the parties but subject to mediation and arbitration' is internally paradoxical language, though it is the familiar AIA formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.4.6 converts the decision into a true final decision if arbitration is not demanded in 30 days, and Agreement 12.2.4 provides a separate route, so finality is defined in three places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is heavily corrupted, but the operative rule — a 30-day demand deadline after a decision that so states, failing which the decision becomes final — turns on conditions stated in the decision itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with 4.6.3's outer limits and Agreement 12.2.4's separate 30-day rule for the final accounting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scanned sentence is broken and the surety notice provision is only partly legible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 16 of the Agreement is blank as to bonds, so 'the surety, if any' may have no referent; 9.6.7 also assumes a possible payment bond.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits a lien claimant to comply with statutory deadlines before resolution of the Claim; clear in purpose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 12.1.4(b) and 12.2.2 build the payment scheme around lien waivers and a lien-free endorsement, which this preserves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scanned text is fragmented, but the clause both requires the parties to 'endeavor to resolve their Claims by mediation' and allows a demand filed concurrently with arbitration yet stayed for 60 days — a mandatory/permissive mix like the clause construed in the worked example.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.6.1 makes mediation a condition precedent to arbitration while Agreement 12.2.4 allows an immediate arbitration demand on the final accounting, so the prerequisites conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fee-sharing, place of mediation and enforceability of agreements reached; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 13.1.1's governing law and the Project location; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The arbitration agreement carries carve-outs ('except Claims relating to aesthetic effect' and Claims waived elsewhere) and a condition precedent expressed through the Architect and mediation, so both what is arbitrable and when are contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.4 permits arbitration of the final accounting without an Architect decision, and 4.4.5-4.4.6 and 4.6.3 set differing preconditions and deadlines.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scanned text is jumbled, but the rule (AAA Construction Industry Rules, demand filed with the other party and the AAA, copy to the Architect) is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.6.1 and 4.6.3, though Agreement 12.2.4's separate demand right has no comparable filing requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three different limits — 4.4.6, 4.6.1, 'a reasonable time', and the applicable statute of limitations as determined under 13.7 — layered in one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 12.2.4's 30-day rule and 13.7.1's accrual rules must all be read together to know when arbitration is time-barred.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Joinder turns on whether a person's presence 'is required if complete relief is to be accorded' and whether an interest is 'not substantial' — indeterminate tests governing who can be brought into an arbitration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Architect is excluded here while 4.2.12-4.2.13 give the Architect decisive roles, and Agreement 12.2.4 contemplates arbitration keyed to the Owner's accountants' report.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short and standard entry-of-judgment clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.6.1-4.6.4; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of Subcontractor excluding separate contractors; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement Article 10 and 6.1.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of Sub-subcontractor; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.1.1 and 9.6.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Failure of the Owner or Architect to reply promptly shall constitute notice of no reasonable objection' turns silence into consent without a defined period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 10.1 gives the Owner the right to determine which bids are accepted and Addendum 6.5 requires at least two bids including Owner-named bidders, so subcontractor selection is governed by three different procedures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable and timely objection' and 'reasonable objection' are standards, but conventionally applied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 10.1's final sentence says the same thing for the Contractor; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Contract Sum adjustment for a rejected but capable Subcontractor is denied if the Contractor has not 'acted promptly and responsively' — a conduct condition on a money remedy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 10.2 gives a different and more specific remedy (Change Order for the bid differential) when the Owner insists on another bidder.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line restriction on changing selected Subcontractors.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.2.1-5.2.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A contingent assignment conditioned on termination for cause, Owner acceptance and surety rights; carefully limited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 13.3 requires assignment of subcontracts on termination for convenience as well, a broader trigger than 14.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The suspension period fill-in is missing from the scanned text, so the trigger for equitable adjustment of subcontractor compensation cannot be read.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Relates to 14.3.2 and Agreement 13.4 on suspension adjustments; consistent in substance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reserves the Owner's right to perform work and award separate contracts, with claims routed to Paragraph 4.3; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 disclaims Owner responsibility for means and methods, and 6.1.4 subjects the Owner's own forces to Contractor-like duties.
